stepNotes.1: The bridge resolves five runtime locations, performs JSON status/serve calls, optionally opens a browser, and forwards status/stop/log commands.
stepNotes.2: Executable selection, inherited environment, child output, UI-password arguments, and the external runtime's JSON are the trust boundaries.
stepNotes.3: Discovery precedence and ENOENT diagnostics are deterministic, errors fail explicitly, an existing server is reused, and missing ports are rejected.
stepNotes.4: At most status plus serve processes are spawned, but stdout/stderr capture has no explicit byte limit.
stepNotes.5: Discovery is testable through injected dependencies; process execution is not injected and leaves exported orchestration hard to isolate.
stepNotes.6: No TODOs or empty catches exist; browser failure is an explicit best-effort branch and __internal is an exercised test seam.
stepNotes.7: Discovery and handoff tests pass, while launch JSON, process failure, port, password, browser, and command-forwarding paths lack direct tests.
stepNotes.8: No finding was accepted; output bounds, argv visibility, and launch coverage are hardening/test notes under the local threat model.
stepNotes.9: The two focused files passed 14 tests and core typechecking passed.
